pairs.question: Quid ergo faciendum est ne pereamus de uia iusta?
pairs.answer: Beati omnes qui confidunt in eum.
pairs.derivation: Author poses the question 'quid ergo faciendum est ne pereamus de uia iusta?' and immediately answers with the scriptural quote (Ps. 2:12) 'beati omnes qui confidunt in eum', which directly answers what must be done (trust in him). Editorial brackets around the quote stripped, words kept. Answer ends at the full stop; the next sentence ('si beati qui confidunt in eum, miseri qui confidunt in se') is elaboration and was cut.

pairs.question: Quare ergo cum timore et tremore eam salutem operor, cum sit in potestate mea operari salutem meam?
pairs.answer: Deus est enim qui operatur in uobis.
pairs.derivation: Author asks why he works salvation with fear and trembling and answers with the Pauline reason (Phil. 2:13) 'deus est enim qui operatur in uobis'. The intervening framing question 'uis audire quare cum timore et tremore?' ('do you want to hear why...?') is a non-answering preamble between question and answer and was cut. Editorial brackets around the answer stripped, words kept. Answer ends at the operative quoted clause; the following 'ideo cum timore et tremore...' is elaboration and was cut.

pairs.question: Si ergo deus est qui operatur in nobis, quare dictum est: uestram ipsorum salutem operamini?
pairs.answer: Quia sic in nobis operatur, ut et nos operemur.
pairs.derivation: Author asks 'quare dictum est...' and answers with the 'quia' clause explaining how God works in us so that we too work. Editorial brackets around the embedded quote 'uestram ipsorum salutem operamini' stripped, words kept. Answer ends at the full stop; the next quote 'adiutor meus esto' begins a new point and was cut.

pairs.question: Nemo te condemnauit?
pairs.derivation: Direct speech in the pericope of the adulteress: Jesus asks 'nemo te condemnauit?' (introduced by 'et aspiciens mulierem dixit', dropped as a speech tag) and the woman answers 'nemo, domine' (introduced by 'et illa', dropped as a speech tag). First of two occurrences chosen as cleanest. Editorial brackets stripped, words kept; first word capitalized.
